terra.problem: Saying the instruction is repeated so nobody is confused supplies a reason the text does not give.
Saying the ovens are kept warm for the same reason, because starting cold puts you behind, assigns a reason to the altar-fire command that the text does not give.
The lunch joke adds a time of day and a view of the altar that the text does not give.
The text does not say the remainder goes straight from the altar to the priests' table.
It identifies every grain offering for a priest with the particular offering described on the day of anointing. Verse 23 gives a general rule without limiting it to that occasion.
The text does not say only a bronze pot is kept, or that the clay pot is broken before the end of the day.
Saying both offerings are eaten by the priests leaves out the sin-offering exception in Leviticus 6:30, where the offering must be burned.
The verse does not mention elders, but 'No middle manager needed' goes further by suggesting no intermediary was involved.

The last sentence places the command on Mount Sinai. The verse says the laws were given there and identifies the day with the command to present offerings in the Wilderness of Sinai; it does not place that command on the mountain.
